description: Runs a declared plan of runs on one card, or of solves of one solver, and seals the rows under one root. A plan is a list of runs, a grid over a base run, or a seeded sample over a base run; a run is a run_trajectory request without domain and card. A plan of solves names solver in place of domain and card and is a list or a grid of solve requests. The answer is small by default: the head, which holds the request, the counts and the dataset_seal, and one summary row per run; answer "states" adds each final state in decimals and "full" gives every row whole, under the same dataset_seal. A row is completed, ended, refused or unadmitted: an ended or a refused row is a run sealed up to its last landed step, and an unadmitted row is a request turned away before computing, with no seal. The seal shows the dataset was not altered after it was sealed. It does not show the engine made it: a row's request sent to run_trajectory gives the run seal to compare. The input schema says how each input is written. On this open connection a dataset is returned inline and holds at most 300 runs (OPEN_MAX_DATASET_ROWS), 1000000 steps in all (OPEN_MAX_DATASET_STEPS), 10000 frames and an answer counted from the plan at 4194304 bytes (OPEN_MAX_DATASET_ANSWER_BYTES) and 42500 characters, up to about 150 summary rows; a plan of solves holds the engine's own 64 and at most 15 s of them, or one, at each solver's measured time, which describe_solver states with the count (OPEN_PLAN_SECONDS). One address holds at most 1 physics permit at a time; a call that finds none is answered "Too many concurrent physics tasks." and nothing waits. An answer is waited for 60 seconds, and long work is stopped there.

inputSchema.description: A plan of runs on one card (domain, card, plan, store and return, all required) or of solves of one solver (solver and plan). Rows <= 100000, steps in total <= 100000000, stored frames <= 16777216; inline: an answer counted from the plan <= 42500 characters, which a plan reaches first, a grid on one axis at about 150 summary rows and a list sooner, its head repeating each run's request (a plan of more than 1000 rows is refused before it is counted, as too large to return inline), and frames <= 10000; solves <= 64. With return "file" the answer is the head and the names of the files stored, on a connection started with a directory for them.

answer.description: Leave out, or "summary", for the head and one short summary row per row: the values it sets, outcome, steps landed, refusal name and seal; "states" adds each run's final state in decimals; "full" gives every row whole. With return "file" the answer is the head and the names of the files whatever this says. Not part of the sealed request. The head and the dataset_seal are the same in all three forms. A summary row holds row, set, outcome, steps_landed, reject and run_seal; an unadmitted row, a request turned away before computing, has no run seal. An inline answer is counted from the plan before anything runs, and one above 42500 characters is refused with what to change.

plan.description: A path names one number: initial.<field>, dt_s, or segments[0].load.<field>, with the segment's number in square brackets and [0], [1] or [2] after a 3-vector field for one of its components. steps and record_every are not paths and cannot vary. Two paths may not set one number. A row whose value is outside a card's bound is unadmitted and the other rows run; a sample's interval or choice outside a bound refuses the plan.

oneOf.description: A list of runs. Each is a run_trajectory request without domain and card.
With solver: a list of solves. Each is a solve request without solver.
A base run (with solver: a base solve request without solver) and axes of explicit values. The rows are the product of the axes, the last axis varying fastest.
A base run and draws from the counter sampler. Row n is worked out without the rows before it.

solver.description: A plan of solves: the solver, in place of domain and card. It takes no store and no return. A plan of solves is answered inline: a list, {"kind":"list","solves":[{"parameters":{...}}]}, or a grid, {"kind":"grid","base":{"parameters":{...}},"axes":[{"path":"parameters.<input>","values":[...]}]}, of at most 64 solves. Each row is a solve request and carries the solution_seal solve gives it, and the rows are sealed under one dataset_seal. verify_dataset verifies a plan of solves by its request and dataset_seal, and validate_series compares one number of its results with measurements.
